title: Review panel, round three: consolidated verdict
verdict: Not ready for public launch. Ready now for stakeholder demonstrations (as a labelled concept on demonstration data) and for a moderated phone usability study in English and Malay with assistive-technology users (MAHB recruits, OOS-15). Not yet ready for a closed KLIA pilot: 4 of the second review's 7 pilot conditions are met (status-line semantics, day-of-travel residuals, one fact one answer, durable commercial measurement); CI on a runner with TBT budgets met or agreed anew, the official flight feed and a named notices owner are not. The panel adds three team conditions for the pilot: no lazy part may replace a page after a failed script fetch and 'Try again' must recover (the saved-flight failure, chair confirmed page-level); the concierge's sticky question box must not hide the focused suggestion (chair confirmed); and the accessibility statement must be true and dated after the fixes. Panel median 75.5% (reviewers 74.0 to 79.5), up 1.0 from 74.5%, all from ai; 3.5 points below Heathrow (79.0%) and 7.5 below the composite (83.0%); the remaining gap is in info, commerce and flight, which depend mainly on MAHB.
caveat: Expert judgement by three independent lenses on a working prototype with demonstration data (no official flight, operations or notices feed); not a user study. No passengers, disabled participants or physical screen readers; Chromium only; no WebKit or real device; one clock time per session (05:46 to 06:47 Kuala Lumpur time, 22 November 2026). ux, flight, mobile, nav, ai and ui are scored as if production data were connected; info and commerce on what exists. Performance is lab data from verification.md round five, not re-measured by any reviewer or the chair (shared machine) and not field data.
method: Median per dimension across three independent third reviews (business, design, inclusion) of the round-five production build; weights ui 10, ux 20, info 15, flight 15, mobile 10, nav 10, ai 10, commerce 5, perf 5; percent = sum(weight x score) / 5. Each reviewer served the build on its own port (3302, 3303, 3304) and did not read the others' third reviews. The chair served it on port 3305 (06:39 to 06:47 MYT), checked points reported by one lens or reported differently, and changed no median.

second_review_weaknesses_status.status: improved, not met; resilience defect exposed

weaknesses: 1. No live operational data and no alert delivery (MAHB: OOS-01, OOS-02, OOS-10). Provider stub; /api/flights mode demo [chair]; notices in code; queue estimates demonstration data; Follow only while a page is open; e-mail a demonstration. Caps info and flight.

2. Content depth, verified prices and operator-grade sourcing (MAHB: OOS-03, 05, 06, 08, 14). 0 of 4 KLIA car-park rates verified; 3 of 39 airports beyond an overview and a board; /en/kch/parking and /en/lgk/transport 404 [chair]; 8 outlets; lounges from third-party sites; MAHB's building described from third-party guides; Malay not natively reviewed.
3. Nothing can be bought (MAHB and partners; team for E-09). Commerce 2.5, level with MAHB today; payment=() and 'unsafe-inline' would block a partner checkout [chair].

4. A failed script fetch blanks the returning passenger's home (team). With a saved flight, 2 of 14 lazy chunks on /en and 2 of 10 on /en/journey each replace the whole <main> with 'Something went wrong'; 'Try again' does not recover after the connection returns [chair]. Verification describes it as card-level.

5. Assisted-travel facts missing and no assistive-technology evidence (MAHB, airlines, Immigration; team with MAHB recruiting). No located accessible toilets, surveyed lifts or step-free status of transport; no assistance service, CARE hours or accessibility contact; no AirAsia, AirAsia X or Batik Air rules; no screen reader, WebKit or disabled participant.

6. The concierge and search still miss intents (team). 'Book me a taxi' lists six modes; 'now' questions ignore queue data; 'Here is what our sources say' leads; departure-autogate questions lead with visitor and arrival-card content in Malay [chair]; turns 500 to 1,163 px. Search: 'pharmacy' 0 results, 'kuching parking' other airports, 'charging' trains, 'lost and found' 39 options, unmarked demonstration lifts lead 'lift' [chair].

7. Release engineering and speed budgets unproven (team) [verification]. CI and WebKit never run on a runner; budget step fails 10 assertions; pooled TBT 227 to 308 ms on eight pages; congested Wi-Fi LCP 2.57 / 2.65 s; first-load JS over 170 KB on 21 of 39 routes; HTML over 40 KB gzip on 14 of 22 pages; worker first visit 61 requests, 643 KB; offline toast waits for the runtime script.

8. Focus defects that contradict the accessibility statement (team). Concierge sticky box covers the focused suggestion at 1280 x 720 [chair] and 1440 x 900 (inclusion); in-page links and palette selections leave focus on <body> or the Search button; statement claims otherwise and predates round five; text-only enlargement beyond 125% breaks the header and bottom bar.

9. Hierarchy, length and density residuals (team). Overview flight search at 2,236 px under a 100-word notice [chair]; about two desktop board rows above a 900 px fold [chair]; facilities 15,451 px and hub up to 19,186 px on a phone; Demo chip per hour group on a filtered board; 9 type sizes on 8 of 280 pages at 390 px; English home h1 a brand line; map route chip over a label.

10. Notice, copy and Malay residuals (team; native review MAHB). 2027 fare badged 'In effect now' and an 'Estimated' chip on a notice [chair]; concierge long-stay card without qualifier; 'no notices right now' on a directory-only airport; Malay mid-word breaks on four pages; 'Penang' versus 'Pulau Pinang'; 'penerbangan simpanan'.
launch_blockers: TEAM [pilot]: Resilience of lazy parts: retryingImport for every React.lazy rendered on load (home saved-flight card, My journey), card-scoped error boundaries, a 'Try again' that re-imports, the saved-flight state in the failed-chunk e2e test; offline toast listener in the shell.

TEAM [pilot]: CI on a runner with WebKit and the chaos and contract tests; TBT budgets met or revised and recorded; then congested Wi-Fi LCP, first-load JS, HTML, byte and worker budgets (A-09, E-01, E-02, E-03, E-06, E-11, E-12).

TEAM [pilot]: Concierge composer must not hide the focused suggestion (re-test at 1280 x 720 and 1440 x 900 with axe); focus to the target for in-page links and palette selections; accessibility statement refreshed, true and dated after the fixes, in both languages.

TEAM: Concierge intent and length: requests it cannot perform, 'now' questions from status and queue lines or 'no live data', lead with the answer, departure-autogate routing in both languages, out-of-scope questions away from the support line, gate letter implies KLIA, B2B 'not published', one lead line and at most two cards on a phone.

TEAM: Search: 'not published for <airport>' with the official link before other airports' pages; vocabulary for pharmacy, charging, ATM, lost and found; down-rank unrelated results; every demonstration place, lifts included, marked illustrative in results and From/To lists.

TEAM: Notice and copy semantics: future-dated changes 'Announced; applies from ...'; no 'Estimated' chip on notices; qualifier on the concierge long-stay card; 'No notices in our sources' for directory-only airports; readable terminal labels.

TEAM: Hierarchy and density: overview flight search above notices on phones; at least five board rows above a 900 px desktop fold; one Demo marker per board view; at most 8 type sizes on every page; shorter facilities, hub and transport pages; map drawing into view on route choice, chip off labels; task-based English h1 (brand owner, OOS-08); 'Saved' state label; filter-strip overflow cue; Fast Track link in the international flight summary.

TEAM: Malay residuals: no mid-word breaks in controls, chips and headings; non-breaking ranges; one name for Pulau Pinang; 'penerbangan yang disimpan'. Recommended: header and bottom bar that survive 200% device text.

TEAM: Low items from verification G8 item 9 (night-board CLS at 1440 px, interaction latency, rate-limit-sensitive e2e test, hreflang in head on 152 of 276, header switcher shift, D-14); per-route CSP and payment policy for any partner checkout (E-09).
TEAM with MAHB: Moderated phone usability study in English and Malay with NVDA, VoiceOver on iOS, TalkBack and magnifier users; MAHB recruits and signs off (OOS-15).
MAHB [pilot]: Official flight feed behind the provider interface, proven against the failure states (OOS-01).
MAHB [pilot: named owner]: Operations status and queue feeds and a notices CMS with bilingual approval, a notice live in under 5 minutes without a deploy, and a named duty owner (OOS-02).
MAHB: Official parking tariff and a booking deep link accepting product, dates and a referral code (OOS-03).
MAHB and partners: Fast Track seller, price, hours and checkpoints; lounge access rules, prices and booking; referral agreements and confirmed conversions (D-02, OOS-04, OOS-13).
MAHB: Content minimum for every international airport, Kuching and Langkawi first; concessionaire directory feed; operating airline and contact for 33 airports (OOS-05, OOS-06).
MAHB: Located accessibility facts for KLIA T1 and T2, the airport assistance service, CARE hours, an accessibility contact with a response time (OOS-07, C-08).
Airlines and Immigration via MAHB: assistance rules for AirAsia, AirAsia X, Batik Air and other carriers (D-04); departure-autogate wording for citizens and counters for older travellers (D-07).
MAHB and partners: Alert delivery by web push including iOS, and by e-mail (OOS-10).
MAHB: Operator-grade sourcing with MAHB as the source for its own building and services; brand, legal and native-Malay review (OOS-08, OOS-14).
MAHB: B2B channels (D-17); hosting edge limits and client-address header, security.txt, field Core Web Vitals on a mid-range Android (OOS-11, OOS-12, OOS-15).
